A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same paper. Their text, equations, seven figures, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original ridge-regression and neural-network simulations. Appendix B adds empirical results on surrogate accuracy, label noise, and random Fourier features.

after.justification: v4 retains the original simulations and empirical findings in Section 5 and Appendix B, including Figures 1–7.

M1.justification: The ridge objective, gradient-descent procedure, feature maps, and neural-network models are unchanged. Corrections to theorem assumptions and a proof's update formula do not establish an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same linear teacher–student problems, random ReLU features, fully trained two-layer ReLU networks, noisy-label regression, and random Fourier features.

E2.justification: The evaluated model and hyperparameter comparisons are unchanged. The newly cited Tikeng Notsawo et al. (2025) is discussed as related theory, not evaluated as an experimental comparator.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B retain the same data generation, sample sizes, model sizes, initialization settings, learning rates, weight decay, and evaluation metrics. Revised step-size inequalities occur in theoretical guarantees, not reported experimental protocols.

E4.justification: The hyperparameter sweeps in Figures 2–4, surrogate-accuracy plateau analysis in Figure 5, and label-noise sensitivity analysis in Figure 6 are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Figure 1 still reports 50 independent runs with independent datasets and initializations; Figure 5 still uses one simulation. Experimental uncertainty reporting is unchanged. The revised failure-probability accounting concerns theoretical proofs.

E6.justification: The embedded plots in Figures 1–7 are identical across versions, and the experimental findings and captions are unchanged. No empirical result entries, numerical outcomes, or trends are added or revised.

T1.justification: v4 makes targeted corrections within the retained theorem framework. Theorem 4.4 replaces the smallest-positive-eigenvalue step-size restriction with a largest-eigenvalue restriction; Theorems 4.2 and 4.6 specify bounds using λ+b². Equation (4), Theorem 4.5, and A.9 replace c²/(λ_min(Σ)²ν²) with c/(λ_min(Σ)ν²), although A.7 retains the old expression. Appendix A adds eventual-generalization, smoothness, and probability-accounting arguments, restores a missing 1/n factor, and changes the squared-loss Lipschitz constant from 2b||θ*|| to 4b||θ*||. Appendix C removes unreferenced standard Lemmas C.2–C.6.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: end-to-end provable grokking in ridge regression, quantitative hyperparameter control, and empirical agreement beyond linear models. The added prior-work comparison contextualizes these existing claims.

C2.justification: The explanations involving data-spanning and orthogonal parameter components, interpretations of hyperparameter effects, and limitations concerning non-realizable regression and neural-network theory are unchanged.

D1.justification: The disclosed feature constructions, initialization distributions, and experimental hyperparameters are unchanged. No hardware, runtime, implementation instructions, or code/data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The introduction and references add Tikeng Notsawo et al. (2025), Grokking beyond the Euclidean norm of model parameters. v4 describes its loss-minimization and regularization phases and positions this paper as providing sharper end-to-end ridge-regression guarantees.

P1.justification: v4 adds a short related-work passage and explanatory proof prose, makes localized wording edits, and shortens Appendix C's heading to Technical Lemmas. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The figures retain their plots, numbering, and captions, but appendix reflow changes their placement: Figure 6 moves from PDF page 22 to page 23, while Figures 5 and 7 shift within their pages. Text and equation placement also changes locally.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens the existing theoretical justification through corrected step-size restrictions, an explicit smoothness argument, and fuller eventual-generalization and probability reasoning in Appendix A. The added related-work comparison also improves attribution. The correction remains incomplete: Theorem A.7 retains the old squared feature-dimension term despite its revision in Equation (4) and A.9. These focused gains support a limited overall improvement.
